description: An empty JSON object, presented under each of the nine recognised artifact filenames and under its own. It parses, it is a supported container, and it carries no envelope any of the nine artifacts must carry -- so every routing of it is a halt. This is the second of the two documents a recognised filename alone would have admitted: the other is a SARIF-family document of an unaccepted version, owned by near-sarif-runs-only.json.
null_field_note: tool, scanner_class, adapter and adapter_invoked are null or false because this fixture's expected outcome is a halt under every name it is presented under, and a halt precedes adapter selection: no adapter is named, none is imported and none is called. Under its own filename the name itself resolves to no tool, so even the tool field has no value to carry.

fixture.authored_note: Authored, not captured. It is deliberately the emptiest well-formed object a runner could leave behind: no version, no runs, no Results, no results, no dependencies, no findings and no top-level array. Nothing in it is a finding, a secret, a credential or a token, and it names no path, so no location of any kind is characterised by it.
fixture.why_this_document: It is what a truncated write, an interrupted serialisation or a hand-copied placeholder looks like: a file whose name says which runner owns it and whose bytes say nothing at all. Routing it on the strength of its name hands an adapter a document with none of the containers it walks, and the adapter then reports zero rows -- a result indistinguishable from a clean scan (AAP 0.5.4). An empty object is also the shortest possible statement of the point, so no incidental key can be mistaken for the thing that made the decision.
fixture.emptiness_is_not_the_fault: The fault is the ABSENT envelope, not the absent records. Its sibling halt-shape-empty-array.json is equally empty and routes normally under gitleaks.json, because a bare array IS gitleaks' whole envelope. The pair is what separates "this document is not that tool's shape" from "this tool found nothing", and only the first is a halt.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Recorded for parity with the positive expected files in this folder; no row below carries it, because rows is empty by expectation.

shape_detection.conjunction: isinstance(doc, Mapping) and doc.get("version") == "2.1.0" and isinstance(doc.get("runs"), list)
shape_detection.is_sarif_derivation: The document is a mapping, so the first condition holds. It carries no keys at all, so doc.get("version") is None and None == "2.1.0" is False, and doc.get("runs") is None and isinstance(None, list) is False. Both halves of the conjunction fail, and no relaxation of either can succeed over a document with nothing to read.

container_check.note: The top level is a JSON object, which IS a container an adapter could own, so REASON_UNSUPPORTED_DOCUMENT_TYPE does not apply. That is deliberate: this fixture must halt for carrying no envelope, not for being structurally impossible, and a fixture that halted on the container check would leave the envelope path untested.

native_shape_detection.authority: shape._NATIVE_ENVELOPE in harness/lib/normalize/shape.py, one entry per canonical tool, each pairing the predicate the router enforces with the prose the halt quotes -- so what is stated and what is enforced cannot drift apart. The markers are AAP 0.5.4's per-shape table: a top-level array for gitleaks, Results for Trivy, results for Checkov and OSV-Scanner, dependencies for Dependency-Check, findings for Joern, and the SARIF conjunction for the three producers, which have no native alternative.
native_shape_detection.checks_note: The document carries no keys, so every marker key is absent; and its top level is an object, so the two array forms -- gitleaks' bare array and Checkov's multi-framework array -- are excluded by type before any key is read. The three SARIF producers are False by construction: their runners write SARIF and nothing else, so their entry admits no native alternative.
native_shape_detection.envelope_only_note: What the router checks is the envelope and only the envelope: the container the per-shape table names is present and is the right JSON type. No record inside it is examined, so every judgement about record structure remains the adapter's -- including the Trivy non-empty-unsupported-section halt, which halt-trivy-unsupported-section.json owns.

under_each_recognised_name.envelope: a SARIF 2.1.0 document -- version == "2.1.0" together with a runs array; this runner writes SARIF and nothing else, so there is no native shape to fall back to
a SARIF 2.1.0 document -- version == "2.1.0" together with a runs array; this runner writes SARIF and nothing else, so there is no native shape to fall back to
a SARIF 2.1.0 document -- version == "2.1.0" together with a runs array; this runner writes SARIF and nothing else, so there is no native shape to fall back to
a JSON array of finding objects at the top level (an empty array is a legitimate clean report)
either one report object carrying a 'results' object, or a non-empty top-level array of such report objects (the multi-framework form)
a report object carrying 'Results', as an array or null (an empty or null 'Results' is a legitimate clean report, but the key's absence means the document is not a Trivy report)
a report object carrying an 'results' array
a report object carrying a 'dependencies' array (an empty array is a legitimate clean report)
a collector object carrying a 'findings' array, as written by harness/lib/joern-scan.sc

under_each_recognised_name_note: Nine entries, one per artifact filename, in canonical tool order. Every outcome is a halt, and the reason splits by whether the name belongs to a SARIF producer: those three runners write SARIF and nothing else, so their artifact failing the conjunction is a producer-or-version condition, while any other recognised name over an unrecognised envelope is a mis-written or mis-placed artifact. Both are halts and each sends a reader somewhere different, which is why they are two reasons rather than one.

under_its_own_name.note: Recorded for completeness, and it is not this fixture's purpose. The name is not one of the nine, so resolve_tool returns None and the name reason is attributed before any envelope is consulted -- the same outcome unknown-shape.json has under its own name. What this fixture exists for is the row above it: the nine claimed names, where the name resolves and the envelope is what refuses.

halt.raised_before: any adapter module is named, imported or called, and before any record traversal of any kind
halt.reason_note: shape.py names four reasons: the unrecognised artifact name, the unsupported document type, a SARIF producer's artifact that is not SARIF, and a recognised native name over an unrecognised envelope. This document's top level is a supported container and each of the nine names resolves, so the first two do not apply and the halt is one of the last two, chosen by whether the claimed name belongs to a SARIF producer.

observed_attributes.artifact_path_note: Whatever subject the caller passed, echoed unchanged -- route never rewrites it. The negative test passes the claimed artifact filename, so no absolute path appears anywhere in this file.
observed_attributes.stem: the canonical tool identifier the claimed name resolved to
observed_attributes.stem_note: For these two reasons the name resolved, so stem carries the canonical identifier -- opengrep, trivy, joern -- rather than the filename. It is the filename only for the unrecognised-name reason, where there is no tool to name.
observed_attributes.expectation: the prose statement of what that tool's artifact must be, taken from shape.native_shape_requirement and non-empty for every one of the nine

halt.observed_attributes_note: These are the attributes the halt carries so a report can quote the observed structure without re-reading the artifact. expectation is the one this outcome adds: a reader is told what shape was required, not only that something was refused.
halt.authority: AAP 0.5.4 -- an artifact matching neither the SARIF shape nor a known native shape is a halt rather than a best-effort parse -- and AAP 0.9.2, which lists it among the conditions that stop the run.

not_a_rejection.reject_classes_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_CLASSES tuple -- a closed set of ten class names, not copied here so the one authority cannot drift into two.
not_a_rejection.statement: The stated outcome is a halt, not a counted rejection: "halt", "UnknownArtifactShape" and each of the four halt reasons shape.py names are provably absent from paths.REJECT_CLASSES, and the test asserts that non-membership programmatically rather than by inspection. A rejection is a per-record outcome inside an adapter that already owns the artifact; this document never reaches an adapter, so there is no record to reject and nothing to count under any class.

parse.note: The fixture is well-formed JSON and json.load succeeds on it. No parser failure is expected and none is stated: malformed input is a different condition, owned by the reject-*-malformed-record fixtures, and conflating the two would let a JSON syntax error pass as a shape halt.
parse.why_well_formedness_is_the_point: A document that fails to parse is stopped by the parser and no shape decision is ever reached. It is precisely a document that parses perfectly and carries nothing that tempts a permissive route: there is no error to report, the container is legitimate, and handing it on "in case it is empty" feels harmless. It is not harmless -- the adapter finds none of its containers and reports zero rows.

counts.reconciliation_identity: not applicable -- the halt precedes any record traversal, so no count unit exists to reconcile against

counts_note: raw_finding_records and raw_count_unit are null rather than 0. A count unit is a property of an artifact's known shape, and this document has none under any of the nine names, so there is nothing for normalize.reconcile.count_records to walk. Writing 0 there would assert that a traversal ran and found nothing, which is the empty-result-set reading this halt exists to prevent.
rows_note: Explicitly empty, and empty for a different reason than a clean scan is empty: the pipeline stopped, it did not look and find nothing. A row count of 0 reported alongside a successful parse status is exactly the silent failure this fixture guards, so only 0 rows together with the named halt is the expected outcome.
row_derivations_note: Empty because no row exists to derive. The positive expected files in this folder carry one derivation per row, field by field; there is nothing here for that section to describe.
guarded_failure: A router that treated a recognised filename as evidence of shape would accept this document nine times over. Each acceptance is silent: the shared SARIF adapter looks for runs and finds nothing; the Trivy adapter looks for Results and finds nothing; the Gitleaks adapter iterates a document that is not an array at all. Every one of them reports success with zero rows, and findings.json is row-only, so a tool contributing no row is invisible in it by construction. The required outcome is the named halt under every name.

assertions: shape.route over this document under each of the nine artifact filenames raises shape.UnknownArtifactShape, and the raised type is exactly that exception rather than a bare KeyError or TypeError.

For the three SARIF producers the reason is shape.REASON_SARIF_PRODUCER_NOT_SARIF; for the other six it is shape.REASON_NATIVE_SHAPE_UNRECOGNIZED. The per-name table above is the record those verdicts are checked against.
exc.stem is the canonical tool identifier the claimed name resolved to, and exc.expectation is a non-empty statement of the required shape.
exc.sarif_detected is False and exc.version is None, and the halt's observed attributes carry the top-level type, the empty key list and the length 0.
shape.matches_native_shape is False for every one of the nine tools over this document, and raises ValueError for a tool outside the nine.
No adapter is invoked: the routing call names, imports and calls no adapter module.
The rows array is empty and the rejection total is 0.
Neither the outcome nor any halt reason is a member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, asserted programmatically over that tuple rather than by inspection.
json.load over the fixture succeeds -- well-formedness is asserted, not assumed, since a fixture that stopped parsing would exercise none of the above.
Under its own filename the halt reason is the unrecognised-name reason instead, which keeps the two attributions distinguishable.
negative_test_contract.mandated_direction_note: AAP 0.5.4 mandates a negative test asserting that a NATIVE artifact does not route to the SARIF adapter; that assertion is owned by the same test file over the native fixtures. This fixture extends it to the direction a recognised name opens: the name identifies the writing runner and is not evidence that the bytes are that runner's shape.

related_fixtures.sibling_container: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/halt-shape-empty-array.json -- the same emptiness in the other container, which routes under gitleaks.json because a bare array is that tool's whole envelope. The pair is what proves the envelope check is not an emptiness check.
related_fixtures.wrong_version_sarif: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/near-sarif-runs-only.json -- carries version "2.1.0-rtm.5" with a real runs array, so under a producer's name it is the other document a recognised filename alone would have admitted.
related_fixtures.fall_through_under_its_own_name: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/unknown-shape.json -- the unrecognised-name halt, with seven plausible keys none of which may cause a match.
related_fixtures.adapter_owned_halt: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/halt-trivy-unsupported-section.json -- a document that PASSES the Trivy envelope, carrying a Results array, and halts inside the adapter on what a section holds. That boundary is unchanged: shape.py validates the envelope, never the records.
related_fixtures.note: Named so a reader can see which layer owns which failure. No fixture's outcome is inferred from another's, and each expected file states its own.

behaviours_not_exercised_by_this_fixture: Row construction of any kind -- no adapter runs, so no field mapping, no severity mapping and no in_scope evaluation is exercised.
Path resolution -- normalize.paths is never called, so no path base, no uriBaseId walk and no non-filesystem coordinate serialisation is exercised.
Per-record rejection -- none of the ten classes in paths.REJECT_CLASSES is reachable from a shape halt.
REASON_UNSUPPORTED_DOCUMENT_TYPE, which needs a top level that is neither a JSON object nor a JSON array; this document's top level is an object.
The valid-SARIF-under-an-unexpected-name halt, whose sarif_detected attribute is True; this document's is False.
A satisfied envelope, which its sibling halt-shape-empty-array.json owns under gitleaks.json.
An adapter's own record-level validation and its own halt, which a document that passes the envelope reaches and this one never does.
Malformed JSON, owned by the reject-*-malformed-record fixtures.
The reconciliation identity, which has no raw finding record count to assert over here.
how_to_check_this_file: Parse the fixture and compare its sha256 and byte size against the fixture block; it holds exactly {} and a trailing newline. Read shape._NATIVE_ENVELOPE and confirm every one of the nine predicates refuses an empty object, then read route and confirm the reason it attributes for a resolved name over a refused envelope. Read paths.py and confirm REJECT_CLASSES holds ten names, none of them the outcome, the exception or either reason recorded here. Then run the negative test: every assertion in negative_test_contract is checkable from this file alone.
prohibitions_observed: No secret value, credential, token or redacted-secret placeholder appears in any field of this file (the tree is committed to git). No finding is judged -- nothing here is called real, important, a false positive or a duplicate. Nothing is deduplicated. No tool's output is characterised against another's: this file describes one document's shape detection and the outcomes it must produce, and nothing else.
